observation_summary: The compiler failed to report a type warning for an invalid property access on an object when the access occurred within an assignment expression. The fix involved removing an incorrect early-return guard that was bypassing the property access validation logic.
reasoning_summary: The fix removed an 'else if' block containing a 'return' statement that was prematurely exiting the property access check logic when the parent node was an assignment. This is a classic case of an incorrect guard (a condition that should not have been there) preventing the execution of necessary validation code. Therefore, it is classified as 'Checking'.
evidence_used: The fix diff shows the removal of: 'else if (n.getJSType() != null && parent.isAssign()) { return; }'
The bug report indicates that the compiler was failing to report a warning for an invalid property access in an assignment context.
The removal of the guard allows the subsequent 'validator.expectNotNullOrUndefined' check to execute, which is the intended behavior for reporting the missing property warning.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix changes the flow of the method, the root cause is specifically the presence of an incorrect conditional guard that bypasses the validation logic, which is the hallmark of a Checking defect.
